title: When I need to manage incident response and post-mortems, I want to automatically log events, timest
job_to_be_done: When I need to manage incident response and post-mortems, I want to automatically log events, timestamps, and actions during incidents, so I can produce accurate post-mortems and prevent repeated incidents.
painful_workflow: Manually logging events, timestamps, and actions taken across Slack, PagerDuty, and internal wikis during an incident. Afterward, spending hours correlating disjointed records to write the post-mortem.
current_workaround: Engineers manually copy-paste Slack messages, PagerDuty alerts, and console outputs into a shared Google Doc during the incident.
verified_facts: The cluster is supported by exactly one signal (SIG-005) drawn from one source (SRC-005), a GitHub issue (per cluster metadata: independent_sources = 1, source_type_count = 1).
The evidence text describes on-call incident coordination involving manual logging of events, timestamps, and actions across Slack, PagerDuty, and internal wikis.
The stated current workaround is manual copy-paste of records into a shared Google Doc during the incident.
The evidence contains no direct user quote, no quantified time or dollar cost, and no engagement metrics.
inferences: Manual correlation of disjointed records likely consumes some engineer time after incidents — the magnitude is unknown but plausibly hours per major incident.

The existence of mature commercial incident-management tools (inference from general market knowledge, not from SIG-005) suggests market-level willingness to pay exists, but is already captured by incumbents, weakening the case for a new product.
A single GitHub issue mention may indicate the topic arises in OSS tooling discussions, but one mention cannot represent a population of buyers.
assumptions: It is assumed (not evidenced) that the GitHub issue author experienced this as painful rather than describing it neutrally.
It is assumed (not evidenced) that incidents recur frequently enough for the target user to prioritize a solution.
It is assumed (not evidenced) that the target user's organization lacks existing tooling like incident.io or PagerDuty post-mortems.
